brief: We run refrigerated deliveries out of one depot in Rotterdam and I need to decide how to handle the 14:00 order cutoff. Make me a page that sets out three ways to implement it so I can compare them and pick one for Monday's planning meeting. Option A: keep the nightly batch planner and add a second run at 13:30. Effort 3 days, about €400/month extra compute, orders that miss 13:30 still wait until the next day. Option B: replace the batch with incremental re-routing every 10 minutes. Effort 4 weeks, €2,850/month, estimated 11% fewer km driven (we drive 18,400 km/week now), risk is that drivers see their routes change mid-shift. Option C: buy the vendor's dynamic dispatch module. 6 weeks to integrate, €6,200/month plus €15,000 setup, 14% fewer km, locks us into their API, 24-month contract. For each option I want effort, running cost, km saved per week, the main risk, and what we would have to undo if it fails. Finish with your recommendation and the one number that would flip it.

A junior on our recipe site sent this change for scaling ingredient quantities. I've written my review notes below. Make a page I can send back to them where each note is tied to the exact line it is about, with a severity on each, so they can work through them one by one. Line numbers are from the new version of the file.

22  def scale_ingredient(item, servings_from, servings_to):
23 +    if servings_from <= 0:
24 +        raise ValueError("servings_from must be positive")
25      factor = servings_to / servings_from
26      qty = item.qty * factor
27 +    if item.unit in ("tsp", "tbsp") and factor > 3:
28 +        qty = qty * 0.85  # seasoning doesn't scale linearly
29 +    if item.unit == "egg":
30 +        qty = max(1, round(qty))
31      return Ingredient(item.name, round(qty, 1), item.unit)

Notes. Line 23: the form posts servings as a string, so this comparison throws on bug #311's input; blocker. Line 27-28: 0.85 is a magic number, and Priya (our test cook) says it is right for salt only, not cinnamon or chilli; major. Line 29: 1,204 of our 3,010 recipes store the unit as "eggs", so this silently never runs; major. Line 30: halving a 1-egg recipe gives 1 egg, which is wrong; ask for a test; minor. Overall the direction is good; say so.

Let me compare my timings against a faster and a slower variant of each, and show the final numbers I settle on so I can copy them into the game.

Write an incident report for Wednesday's firmware rollout of our smart thermostats, for our leadership team and our two utility partners. Facts: version 3.2.1 started rolling out at 09:00 UTC to 5% of 48,000 devices and went to 25% at 09:40. At 10:25 support got the first tickets: thermostats stuck on "Updating" with the heating off. By 11:05 there were 312 tickets and we paused the rollout at 31% (about 14,900 devices). Cause: the new bootloader checks a flash checksum at one offset, but hardware rev B units store that partition at a different offset, so 2,140 rev B units failed to boot after the update and fell back to safe mode (heating holds at 16 C frost protection). Rev A and C were fine. A remote rollback pushed 12:30-14:10 recovered 1,980; 160 need a manual reset and phone support is calling them. Forecast low Thursday night is 3 C. Why we missed it: there were no rev B units in staging. Actions: add rev B to staging (Priya, Oct 24); 1% canary for 24 hours before any larger step (Marcus, done); credit partners for 2 days of billing events (Jo, Oct 28). The partners care about customer comfort and safety impact.

New staff keep asking how a donation turns into a tax receipt at Riverside Literacy Trust, so I want a page that explains the process, including every branch and decision. A donor gives online, by cheque, or at an event. Online gifts arrive instantly through the payment provider; cheques are entered by the office within 3 working days; event cash goes in the safe and is counted by two people the next morning. Every gift is entered in the donor database with a gift type. Then a decision: is the gift £250 or more? If yes, the finance manager approves it before a receipt goes out (target 2 working days). If under £250, the receipt is automatic. Another decision: is the donor in the UK and did they tick Gift Aid? If yes, we add the gift to the monthly Gift Aid claim submitted on the 5th, worth 25% on top; if no, nothing is claimed. If the address is missing, the gift goes to a chase list reviewed on Fridays and the receipt waits. Receipts are emailed, or posted if there is no email. Last year we processed 6,420 gifts totalling £318,775, and 38% carried Gift Aid. Put the numbers where they help a newcomer.

Our greenhouse has four irrigation zones on one pump and I keep breaking the schedule when I edit it by hand. Build me a page to change the schedule safely. Current schedule: Zone 1 "Tomatoes", starts 05:30, 20 minutes, daily. Zone 2 "Peppers", 05:45, 15 minutes, Mon/Wed/Fri. Zone 3 "Seedlings", 06:00, 10 minutes, runs twice a day (06:00 and 16:00), daily. Zone 4 "Herb bench", 06:10, 12 minutes, daily. Rules: the pump delivers 12 litres per minute and runs only one zone at a time, so runs must not overlap; no single run may be longer than 45 minutes; total water per day can't exceed 900 litres; nothing may start between 11:00 and 15:00 because of the heat; every zone name must be unique and not blank. Right now Zones 1 and 2 overlap. Let me change names, start times, durations and days, show clearly what is broken and why, and show litres used on each day of the week. Only when the schedule is valid should I be able to copy the final schedule out to paste into the controller's settings.
